sections.h2: Which Laurel County offices touch a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Three offices in and around London split the job. One values the property, one collects the money, and one inherits whatever stays unpaid. Calling the wrong one costs a seller time, so here is who does what.

  • Property Valuation Administrator (PVA): Room 127 at 101 S. Main St. Call (606) 864-2889. The office closes at 4:30 Monday through Friday, and its website runs parcel searches by street address, owner name or parcel number.
  • Sheriff: 1380 East Hwy 192. Call 606-864-6600. Counter service ends at 4:00 on weekdays, and Saturday and Sunday are closed.
  • County Clerk: Room 203 at the same Main Street address, phone (606) 864-5158. The clerk receives delinquent bills and runs the sale of the liens.

The rate differs by taxing district, so get the figure for your own parcel from the sheriff or the PVA.

sections.h2: What should an owner know about Laurel County itself?
sections.html:
The state cut Laurel County out of four older counties in December 1825, and it now covers about 434 square miles of land. London is the seat. Corbin lies mostly across the border in Whitley County. Pieces of the Daniel Boone National Forest and Laurel River Lake sit within its borders. History buffs know it for the Civil War fight at Wildcat Mountain, and visitors for the first Kentucky Fried Chicken cafe north of Corbin and the World Chicken Festival in London.

  • Population: an estimated 63,746 in July 2025, up from 62,613 in 2020 and 58,849 in 2010, with a 2020 density of 144 residents per square mile.
  • Older residents: 19.1 percent are 65 or above, the group that can claim the homestead exemption described below, and 16.6 percent of residents under 65 report a disability.
  • Housing: 27,063 units, 23,996 households, 71.6 percent owned by their occupants.
  • Middle home value $159,500. Owners with a mortgage carry median monthly costs of $1,239, and owners without one report $382.
  • The Census Bureau counted 21 building permits for the county in 2025.
  • Jobs: 1,272 employer establishments and 23,992 workers in 2023, with retail sales near $1.68 billion in 2022.
  • Money and movement: median household income of $57,771, a 22.6 minute average commute, and 2.57 people per household.

sections.h2: What are the Laurel County payment dates and penalties?
sections.html:
The assessment date is New Year's Day, and the tax for that year is due at the sheriff's office before December 31 ends. KRS 134.015 turns the calendar into money.

  • A bill paid in full by November 1 shrinks by 2 percent.
  • Between November 2 and December 31 the full printed amount is owed.
  • January adds 5 percent on top.
  • February and later add 10 percent.

If bills are late getting out, the state can swap in a shifted timetable with a discount month followed by a face-value month. The sheriff's page lists three routes: walk in, mail a check, or leave one in the box on the building's front. Cards work at the office only. Cash does not belong in either, and a mailed receipt needs an envelope you have addressed and stamped.

sections.h2: How can a Laurel County owner contest a value?
sections.html:
Start by talking to the PVA or a deputy, since the local board will not hear an owner who skipped that step. Anyone may read the real property roll for thirteen days from the first Monday of May, six days a week. File the written appeal with the county clerk by close of business on the workday after viewing ends.

The board convenes about a month after viewing ends. Bring proof such as sales of similar houses, an insurance policy, what the building cost, or a description of the lot. An appeal without documents is denied, and an owner who misses the hearing cannot take the dispute on to the Kentucky Claims Commission. Bills that print mid-dispute use the owner's number, and a supplemental bill follows if the board's value comes out higher.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for homestead relief in Laurel County?
sections.html:
For the 2025 and 2026 assessment years the state deducts $49,100 from the home's assessment. On a $200,000 house the taxable figure falls to $150,900. Owners who are 65 or older qualify, and so do owners classified as totally disabled. In Laurel County 19.1 percent of residents are 65 or older, so a share of sellers may have it on file already.

Applications are filed at the PVA's Room 127 office, along with documents showing age or disability. A claim based on disability is renewed yearly. Veterans with a service connected disability skip the renewal, as do owners Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems has found permanently and totally disabled. Ask the PVA how the exemption is treated after the house is sold.

sections.h2: What does a delinquent Laurel County tax bill turn into?
sections.html:
Once collection closes on April 15, every open bill goes from the sheriff to the clerk, who records a lien and renames the bill a certificate of delinquency. Interest accrues at 1 percent per month, and a partial month counts in full. In the state's sample, a $1,000 bill reaches $1,254 at the handoff on an assumed 4 percent sheriff commission, and the clerk's and county attorney's shares push it higher with each notice.

A $1,000 Kentucky bill as it ages in the clerk's office (Department of Revenue examples)
When it is settledAmount
On the day the sheriff transfers it$1,254.00
Within five business days of the transfer$1,387.79
After the county attorney's first letter$1,611.30
In May$1,627.61
After the June newspaper listing$1,659.90
By an outside buyer at the sale$1,704.21

The county attorney mails a first notice within 30 days of the transfer and a second within 60 days, and the second names the sale date. The clerk must hold the sale at least 90 and at most 135 days after the transfer, and a third party who buys the certificate may add substantial fees of its own. The Laurel County Clerk's notice for the 2026 sale had outside buyers registering August 17 through August 31 with a deposit of 25 percent of their list value, and that registration window is over. The same notice set the 2026 sale lottery for September 9 at 9:00 a.m. in the clerk's Delinquent Tax Department, also past. KRS 134.015 lets that lien last eleven years, whoever holds title.

sections.h2: What tax steps should a Laurel County seller finish before listing?
sections.html:
• Get a statement from the sheriff showing this year's bill and any older year still open.
  • Ask the clerk's delinquent tax staff whether a certificate already exists against the parcel.
  • Check the PVA website to confirm owner name, parcel number and assessed value.
  • Use the bill search links on the sheriff's website to pull the parcel's tax history, and bring the printout to the listing appointment.
  • If you hold the homestead exemption, ask the PVA what happens to it at the sale.
  • Write the split of the current year's bill into the contract so the closing agent knows each side's share.

Sellers who want to skip repairs can request a direct offer. Any tax still owed is paid out of the proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Where does a Laurel County owner pay the tax bill?
faqs.a: At the sheriff's office, 1380 East Hwy 192, London. Payment is accepted at the counter with a card, by mailed check and at the drop box outside.

faqs.q: How big is the early payment discount in Laurel County?
faqs.a: Two percent off, when the sheriff receives the full bill by November 1. After that the printed amount applies through December.

faqs.q: Which office handles a disagreement over value?
faqs.a: Start with the PVA's office at (606) 864-2889. A meeting there is required before an appeal can be filed.

faqs.q: How much does the Kentucky homestead exemption take off?
faqs.a: It deducts $49,100 from the assessed value for qualifying owners. Applications go to the PVA.

faqs.q: Does a tax lien stay with the property after a sale?
faqs.a: Yes. KRS 134.015 lets a delinquent tax lien run for eleven years regardless of who owns the land, so a buyer's title agent searches for it.
